A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable main text, equations, Tables 1–7, Figures 1–2, and Appendices A–C. Corresponding content can be reliably matched throughout.

before.justification: v2 reports original RLSA and RLNN experiments on maximum independent set, maximum clique, and maximum cut, including ablations in Section 5.3 and longer-run comparisons in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains the original solver evaluations, ablations, training curves, and longer-run comparisons reported in Section 5 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: Equation 14 and Algorithm 1, line 7 replace minus epsilon with plus epsilon in the sigmoid argument. This changes the stated RLSA flip probabilities when epsilon is positive. The broader RLD framework, RLNN procedure, and Appendix C's epsilon-free sample code remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MIS on RB and ER graphs, maximum clique on RB graphs, and maximum cut on BA graphs, retaining the same size ranges and large-ER transfer-testing scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains identical in the corresponding main-result tables, ablations, and Appendix B comparisons. This includes iSCO, the neural and operations-research baselines, discrete LD, and RLNN without regularization.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix A retain the same data splits, sample counts, metrics, model configuration, training budgets, and sampling settings. Appendix B still evaluates both RLSA and iSCO with ten times more steps.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 retains the discrete-LD step-size comparison and RLNN regularization ablation, with unchanged Figures 1–2 and Table 3. Appendix B's analysis of performance under longer runtime is also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same parallel-process counts and describe Figure 1 as showing means and standard deviations across test instances. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1–3 and 6–7 and both figure images are unchanged. For example, RLSA's MIS RB-[200–300] result remains size 19.97 in 35 seconds, and its ten-times-step result remains 20.10 in 6.98 minutes.

T1.justification: Equation 12 restores the missing gradient, changing s_tau(x) = log p_tau(x) to s_tau(x) = ∇log p_tau(x). Section 4.2 also changes the inverse-step-size numerator from Delta_(d) + epsilon to Delta_(d) - epsilon, consistently with Equation 14. These are localized mathematical corrections; no proofs or broader theoretical developments are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning escaping local optima, the RLSA and RLNN solvers, competitive solution quality, and computational efficiency.

C2.justification: The explanations of local-optimum escape, the connection to normalized gradient descent, training efficiency, and the MCut ablation exception are unchanged. Section 6 retains the limitations concerning binary variables, untested broader problem classes, and missing theoretical understanding.

D1.justification: The hardware, hyperparameters, optimizer, numerical precision, training-time information, postprocessing instructions, and code-access information are unchanged. Appendices A and C retain the same implementation details and sample-code content.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and substantive positioning relative to prior sampling and neural methods are unchanged. Adding 'Solvers' to the Section 2.1 heading does not alter that positioning.

P1.justification: Section 2.1 is renamed from 'Simulated Annealing for CO' to 'Simulated Annealing Solvers for CO', and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Appendix C changes code-listing presentation: previously gray docstrings become red, with visible whitespace markers. Scientific figures, table structures, captions, and their placement are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves mathematical accuracy by restoring the score gradient in Equation 12 and revising the epsilon cutoff to favor the d-th-ranked flip, consistent with the intended update. These limited corrections outweigh the small visual clutter introduced in Appendix C. Empirical evidence and implementation documentation remain unchanged.
